module_microarchitecture.name: adaptive_aero_control_top
module_microarchitecture.implementation_style: Top-level synchronous integration wrapper that instantiates the CSR/MMIO decode, streaming transport, surrogate/reference evaluator, safety bounding stage, and technology-neutral history/payload storage controller exactly as named in the spec.
module_microarchitecture.control_strategy: Use MMIO-programmed configuration to enable the datapath, select surrogate/mode policy, set timeout and stale limits, define actuator bounds, and provide memory base selectors; route transport and validation status into the safety stage; expose only the specified top-level outputs and never synthesize a fallback command.
module_microarchitecture.state_strategy: Keep only minimal top-level glue state such as interconnect handoff and registered status fanout if needed; all firmware-visible configuration, fault latch semantics, freshness tracking, and command validity gating remain in the declared child partitions.
module_microarchitecture.output_strategy: Drive all top-level outputs from the named child modules with real RTL sources: MMIO responses from the CSR block, transport handshakes from the transport block, and actuator/status/fault outputs from the safety bounding block.
ownership_notes: The top module is the required synthesizable design top and must not be substituted by any leaf, telemetry, or register-bank module.
It owns integration only and does not redefine ports, filenames, or module names.
Top-level outputs must have actual RTL drivers and must not be tied only to child inputs.

module_microarchitecture.name: adaptive_aero_mmio_csr
module_microarchitecture.implementation_style: Single-cycle decode-oriented CSR/MMIO block with explicit register map implementation for control, timeout, stale limit, bounds, memory bases, and status readback.
module_microarchitecture.control_strategy: Decode every register listed in register_contract, accept writes to writable fields, return current committed values and status on reads, and emit a one-cycle clear-fault semantic to the safety stage when the software writes the clear bit.
module_microarchitecture.state_strategy: Store the firmware-visible configuration fields as registered CSR state; maintain only the committed register contents and no inaccessible software-visible state.
module_microarchitecture.output_strategy: Provide mmio_rdata, mmio_ready, and mmio_error directly from the decode logic and fan out configuration/status signals to the rest of the controller using the explicit inter-module signals defined in the spec.
ownership_notes: Owns the firmware-visible control plane and must not be replaced by streaming transport.
Every declared register must be reachable through RTL decode.
No internal state may be described as software-visible unless it is explicitly in the register_contract.

module_microarchitecture.name: adaptive_aero_transport
module_microarchitecture.implementation_style: Small handshake/packing engine that forms request payloads from explicit semantic inputs, manages in-flight request/response status, and forwards response payloads to downstream validation.
module_microarchitecture.control_strategy: When enabled and a packet is available, assert model_req_valid with model_req_data; consume model_req_ready as an input; accept model_rsp_valid/model_rsp_data as inputs; assert model_rsp_ready only when able to take a response beat; report request_busy, response_valid, response_data, and response_stale as transport status.
module_microarchitecture.state_strategy: Keep only minimal packet staging and transaction-progress state needed for one in-flight model exchange and freshness detection; avoid unnecessary FSM complexity beyond idle/requested/waiting/response-accepted behavior if sequential handshaking requires it.
module_microarchitecture.output_strategy: Drive the external transport pins in the mandated direction contract and provide staged response/status outputs to the evaluator block without affecting actuator outputs directly.
ownership_notes: Owns streaming transport only and does not generate actuator commands.
Must not drive model_req_ready, model_rsp_valid, or model_rsp_data.
Transport may coexist with MMIO but cannot replace it.

module_microarchitecture.name: adaptive_aero_surrogate_reference
module_microarchitecture.implementation_style: Combinational-plus-registered evaluator that interprets the surrogate response payload, produces a transparent reference command path, and compares the two within the configured operating envelope.
module_microarchitecture.control_strategy: Use cfg_enable, cfg_mode_select, cfg_tilt_limit, and cfg_deflection_limit to select the eligible command candidate and to determine whether the response is valid, stale, or out of envelope; if response_stale is asserted, invalidate the result and flag error.
module_microarchitecture.state_strategy: Keep only the minimum latched context needed for evaluation consistency, such as the latest accepted response interpretation or derived request-pack fields; do not introduce a substitute controller or fallback path.
module_microarchitecture.output_strategy: Emit explicit packed request-state fields for the transport engine, produce surrogate and reference command candidates as separate signals, and raise validation_valid/validation_error/validation_delta_code for the safety stage.
ownership_notes: This is the transparent reference and physics-based surrogate partition, not a fallback controller.
Surrogate and reference outputs must remain distinct semantic signals.
No substitute command may be generated when validation fails.

module_microarchitecture.name: adaptive_aero_safety_bounding
module_microarchitecture.implementation_style: Final safety gate and command-limiting stage that clamps candidate commands to configured bounds and suppresses validity when any invalid, stale, timeout, reset, or fault condition is present.
module_microarchitecture.control_strategy: Select the validated command candidate, bound tilt/deflection to cfg_tilt_limit/cfg_deflection_limit, assert actuator_cmd_valid only when validation_valid is true and no fault/stale/timeout condition is active, and latch fault_latched until explicit clear-fault semantics are acknowledged.
module_microarchitecture.state_strategy: Retain only latched fault and status state plus any internal safe bounded values necessary for deterministic readback; hold last safe bounded values if needed internally but never assert validity without a fresh accepted command.
module_microarchitecture.output_strategy: Drive actuator_cmd_valid, actuator_cmd_tilt, actuator_cmd_deflection, actuator_cmd_mode, fault_latched, status_valid, status_code, status_fault_latched, status_timeout_active, and status_stale_active as the final externally visible actuation and status interface.
ownership_notes: Owns the final actuation gate and fault-latching behavior.
Must deassert validity rather than substituting a fallback command.

module_microarchitecture.name: adaptive_aero_history_store
module_microarchitecture.implementation_style: Technology-neutral inferred-memory wrapper intended for FPGA block RAM mapping, with simple busy signaling and base-address selection driven by firmware configuration.
module_microarchitecture.control_strategy: Use cfg_history_base and cfg_payload_base to select the addressed storage windows and expose access sequencing through history_busy and payload_busy without altering control or safety decisions.
module_microarchitecture.state_strategy: Implement bulk history/payload storage as a synchronous inferred memory structure, not as a flattened register bank; keep only the minimal address/control state required for safe access sequencing.
module_microarchitecture.output_strategy: Return stored read data through the declared functional memory interface inside the wrapper contract and report simple busy indicators for concurrent-access protection.
ownership_notes: Owns bulk storage control only and does not affect actuator safety or transport direction.
The memory implementation must remain technology-neutral and block-RAM friendly.
No flattened scalar-register substitute storage may be created.

fsm_intent.description: No standalone top-level FSM is implied beyond the simple synchronous integration of the named submodules; any sequencing is delegated to the transport, CSR, and safety blocks.
Register decode is preferred over a complex FSM; MMIO transactions can be handled with straightforward valid/ready decode and registered write/read behavior.
A minimal handshake sequence is implied for request formation and response acceptance, likely using a small idle/in-flight/response-accepted sequencing structure rather than a complex FSM.
The evaluator is primarily combinational/registered arithmetic and validation logic; no complex FSM is clearly required.
Safety gating is dominated by registered status and latch behavior rather than an explicit complex FSM.
Bulk memory access control is expected to use simple synchronous address/control sequencing rather than an FSM.

internal_storage: freshness counter or age tracker if needed
last safe bounded command if retained internally
synchronous inferred memory for bulk history
synchronous inferred memory for bulk payload snapshots

sequencing_notes: Firmware first programs CTRL, timeout, stale limit, bounds, and storage base registers through the MMIO/CSR interface.
The transport engine forms a request only when enabled and when the semantic request packet is available; the request side uses valid/data outputs and consumes request-ready as input.
The response side accepts response-valid/data as inputs and emits response-ready as output, then forwards the accepted payload to the evaluator.
The surrogate/reference evaluator compares the accepted response against the transparent reference and emits validation and candidate-command signals.
The safety stage clamps the selected command to the configured envelope and asserts actuator validity only for fresh, validated, non-faulted conditions.
On invalid, stale, timeout, reset, or fault conditions, actuator validity is deasserted and the fault remains latched for software handling; no alternate command is synthesized.
Bulk storage is addressed through firmware-controlled base fields and remains memory-wrapper backed rather than flattened into registers.
timing_notes: All modules are synchronous to clk with active-low reset_n.
Top-level outputs must be driven by actual RTL sources and should not depend on child-input-only connections.
MMIO ready/error and readback should be generated by the CSR decode path with straightforward transaction semantics.

The transport and safety paths should use minimal registered sequencing sufficient for handshake, freshness, and fault-latch behavior; no complex FSM is implied unless needed for a valid one-request/one-response protocol.
Response freshness and timeout handling should be bounded by the configured cycle counters from the CSR block.
The memory wrapper should infer to synchronous block RAM-friendly storage in FPGA flow and should not be implemented as a flat register array.
consistency_notes: No hierarchy, ports, or filenames may differ from digital_spec_json.
